title: Parker's Amazing Body Balance
markdown:
As they climbed, the air grew thin. Parker felt his lungs struggle. His heart thumped a fast beat against the quiet mountain. “It’s like a clever machine, Professor,” he panted, voice barely a whisper against the wind. “It tries to stay steady even when everything around it changes. A tricky balance.”

Professor Calder smiled and let the young scholar think. Glow trotted ahead, then waited, as cats do when the altitude has opinions.

The mountain showed its tougher side. A sharp cold wind swept down, biting bone, stealing warmth. Parker shivered, teeth chattering a fast rhythm. Glow, fur puffed like a startled ball, snuggled close to his boots. Her purr was a low comforting hum, a small engine that refused to be impressed by weather.

“See?” Calder’s voice was steady, an old strong tree. “Your body knows. That shiver is a small fire starting inside, trying to make heat. A warning and a solution.”

Parker felt a shiver that was not only cold. Sudden bright understanding. Not merely feeling chilled. A battle to stay balanced, muscles stoking themselves without a committee.

The climb continued. They came out of a dark ravine into sun that beat fiercely. Heat rose from the rocks; the air danced and shimmered. Parker’s skin went hot, throat dry. He breathed fast, chest rising and falling. “It’s happening again. The opposite. Working to cool me. Sweat. Fast breathing. Getting rid of extra heat before I overheat.”

Calder nodded, eyes shining. “Deep chill or scorching sun. The body hunts the middle ground. Always adjusting to the world outside. A quiet dance to keep the inside just right.”

They paused in the shade of a leaning slab so Glow could pretend she had chosen the rest. Parker drank, counted his pulse, watched it settle a little once the wind and the sun stopped arguing in the same minute.

Finally they stood on the rocky top, the world a colourful blanket below. Wind sang. Sun felt like a warm hug that, a ravine ago, had been an enemy. Parker looked at his hands, at Glow stretching lazily, at Calder solid as the mountain.

“Homeostasis,” he said, the word like a stone that fitted the palm. “Temperature. Water. The self, kept steady. Not only surviving. Thriving by staying in range.”

Calder set a hand on his shoulder, years of encouragement in it. He did not call it a secret told by every breath, or fill the summit with incredible mysteries. “A dance, yes. Every shiver. Every sweat. Resilient, and ordinary, which is the impressive part.”

The climb ended. Parker felt a little sad the ascent was over, and proud of the data his own skin had provided. Even when things felt tough, the body worked to keep him safe and steady. He did not look forward to quiet miracles as a speech. He wrote cold-shiver / heat-sweat / thin-air-heart in the margin of Calder’s map, tucked Glow inside his jacket for the first switchbacks down, and let the mountain keep its wind, which had been, all along, a variable his blood already knew how to meet.
